title: Real Madrid Player Ratings vs. AEK Athens: Another Magical Madrid European Comeback
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas3:13 PM ESTFederico Valverde (middle) was the hero of Real Madrid’s comeback.  / Milos Bicanski/Getty ImagesReal Madrid came from behind twice to defeat AEK Athens 3–2 on Wednesday night, with a stunning Federico Valverde stoppage-time strike completing the comeback.

The hosts were very much amped up for Real Madrid's visit and took the game to the visitors. After missing two early chances, Aboubakary Koïta made a nice move on Marc Cucurella and fired a near-post rocket that beat Thibaut Courtois, giving AEK Athens the lead just 12 minutes in.

Real Madrid survived the early onslaught and slowly grew into the game. Then, after getting an equalizer disallowed for a marginal offside, Jude Bellingham leveled the scoring with a beautiful backheel finish just past the 30 minute-mark. It was a goal at the reach of only the world’s best.

The second half was a mud fight between two teams that struggled to create much of anything in attack. But when Los Blancos seemed to be in control, an electrifying counter attack saw Koïta turn provider, sliding a low cross for Stavros Pilios to fire the hosts ahead in the 75th minute.

But the joy lasted just three minutes, as a brilliant Bellingham pass allowed Denzel Dumfries to square a ball for Kylian Mbappé, who overcame what had been a difficult night with a much-needed equalizer.

The 15-time European champions put the pressure on in the dying minutes and finally, Valverde unleashed a trademark long-distance missile that found the top corner, winning the game for Jose Mourinho’s side with just seconds remaining.
The vintage Champions League comeback sees Real Madrid remain perfect in the league phase standings and extend their winning streak to seven games.

Bernardo Silva pulled the strings on Wednesday night.  / Milos Bicanski/Getty Images Bernardo Silva was arguably Real Madrid’s best player on the pitch. Tasked with dictating his team’s possessions, the Portuguese was at his vintage best. His intelligent positioning allowed him to always be an outlet and he dominated on the ball. Silva crashed the box at times—a wrinkle Mourinho has added to his role—but also had the stamina to track back and help his backline. He delivered a complete performance.

Superlatives are starting to run out when describing Jude Bellingham, a player capable of overcoming his context and still producing. The Englishman’s knack of lifting his team up through adversity was on full display again. His equalizer was a thing of beauty, and his through ball to set up Madrid’s second was just as good.
Then, when Real Madrid needed a hero, it was captain Fede Valverde who came to the rescue. The Uruguayan won the game with a majestic strike, one of the best goals of the Champions League season.

Vinícius Júnior never got tired of running into defenders.  / Aris Messinis/AFP/Getty ImagesIt’s a broken record at this point, but it’s simply unbelievable how innocuous Vinícius Júnior looks at the moment. The Brazilian’s talent is world-class, but his confidence seems completely shot. His presence on the pitch instantly makes Yan Diomande more uncomfortable, given he’s forced to operate on the right. Right now, Vinícius Jr worsens Real Madrid’s attack because of his dreadful form and how he impacts those around him.

Not even an assist could rescue Denzel Dumfries’s latest frustrating performance. He once again pushed forward with force at times, but seems clueless when it comes to deciding what to do with the ball once he gets to a potentially threatening position—unless Mbappé is wide open inside the six-yard box.
Defensively, he was Madrid’s weakest link—and that’s saying something considering how shaky Éder Militão, Antonio Rüdiger and Marc Cucurella looked.
Jude Bellingham delivered when Real Madrid needed him most—again.  / Adam Pretty/UEFA/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Thibaut Courtois—6.1: Had it not been for Courtois’s greatness, Los Blancos would’ve conceded at least three goals before the 20 minute-mark.

RB: Denzel Dumfries—7.2: A defensive liability from the start. The Dutchman struggled one-on-one against AEK’s forwards and was caught out of position multiple times. He got an assist but outside of that, couldn’t even get his throw-ins right.
CB: Éder Militão—7.5: It was the Brazilian’s first start of the campaign and it showed. Militão looked slow and rusty, and Luka Jović was able to exploit his subpar form.

CB: Antonio Rüdiger—6.9: Militão at least has his lack of playing time as an excuse for his poor performance. Rüdiger, though, equally struggled against Jović and more so against Mijat Gaćinović, with the pair turning him around with clever moves to get a shot away.

LB: Marc Cucurella—8.1: Clumsy from Cucurella, who wasn’t tight enough on Koïta and then bit on his dribble, giving him all the space he needed to fire his side ahead. Redeemed himself when he assisted Bellingham’s equalizer, but he still was far from great and incessantly fouled opponents all game.
